name: Sailfin packbeast

baseline.name: Sailfin packbeast
baseline.look: Six-legged dune herbivore with a foldable cooling sail and broad padded feet.
baseline.ecology: Domestic herds graze salt grass near oasis margins.
baseline.limit: Needs water and rest; refuses unstable glass crust.
baseline.encounter: Caravan teams treat refusal as information, not disobedience.
baseline.scale_note: Adult representative staging envelope; individuals vary by up to 10%. Not shown at common scale on the art plate.

daily: A packbeast grazes salt grass, chews slowly and folds its cooling sail in narrow shade. Six broad padded feet spread weight. Caravans plan feed, rest and water as actual cargo costs.
cycle: Herds remain near oasis margins during vulnerable young-rearing periods. Training builds tolerance for harness and routine; it does not remove fear or fatigue.
signs: A lowered head and widely planted front pair often precede refusal. A damaged harness can cause the same behavior as unstable crust, so handlers inspect both.
escalation: Slows -> stops -> turns head toward handler -> backs away under pressure. It is not stubborn comic machinery that moves when struck.
community: Ossara handlers can stop a departure without the merchant’s consent. Their reputation rests on reading animals accurately, not claiming they are infallible.
scene: An impatient courier blames the lead animal. Maela first checks the harness, then discovers hollow glass under the shortcut; neither explanation is assumed in advance.
motion: Maintain six contact points with a readable alternating gait. Fold the sail along consistent ribs. Cargo and harness must remain attached to the same landmarks.
sounds: Breath, chewing and low contact calls. No speaking role or transformation into a warrior.
rule: Domestic herbivore with six legs, broad padded feet and foldable sail. Needs water and rest; never an inexhaustible engine.
canon_status: Additive ecology and production guidance; proposed scene remains unadopted.
